title: Vinted Alternatives: 7 Apps Like Vinted for Buying & Selling Second-Hand Clothes (UK)
intro: Vinted is the UK's biggest second-hand fashion marketplace, but it's not the only one — and the right alternative depends on what you're selling and who you want to reach. This guide compares the main Vinted alternatives (Depop, eBay, Facebook Marketplace and more) on fees, audience and what they're best for.

body.heading: The short answer: Depop and eBay are the closest alternatives
paragraphs: If you're looking for an app that works like Vinted — list second-hand clothes, chat with buyers, ship with integrated labels — the two closest alternatives in the UK are Depop and eBay. Both are now free to sell on for casual sellers, and each has a slightly different audience.

Vinted itself remains the most fashion-focused of the three with the simplest fee structure, but it isn't right for every seller or every item. The choice comes down to audience, fees, and what you're actually selling.
This guide walks through the main alternatives in the UK and what each one is genuinely good for.

body.heading: Depop — the closest like-for-like alternative
paragraphs: Depop is the most direct Vinted competitor: a mobile-first, fashion-focused marketplace with a younger, trend-driven audience. It skews towards vintage, streetwear and Y2K styles, and its seller fees dropped to £0 in 2026 (with a 2.9% + £0.30 payment processing fee), making it genuinely competitive on price.

Where Depop differs from Vinted is tone and audience. Depop is more curated and more about personal style, while Vinted is more mass-market and budget-driven. If you're selling unique vintage or streetwear, Depop's audience may value it more.
We've written a full breakdown of the two in our [Vinted vs Depop comparison](/guides/vinted-vs-depop).

body.heading: eBay — the broadest reach, now free too
paragraphs: eBay is the generalist alternative. It sells everything, not just clothes, and its audience is made up of intent-driven searchers rather than casual browsers. Since October 2024, eBay UK has been free for private sellers — 300 free listings a month with no final value fees — so it's now genuinely competitive with Vinted on cost.

The trade-off is that eBay is less fashion-focused. It's stronger for collectibles, electronics, vintage and non-clothing items, and weaker for everyday branded clothing than Vinted. For the full comparison, see [Vinted vs eBay](/guides/vinted-vs-ebay).

body.heading: Facebook Marketplace — best for local, cash, bulky items
paragraphs: Facebook Marketplace isn't a fashion marketplace, but it's a real alternative for certain things: bulky items, homeware, furniture, and local cash sales with no postage at all. There are no seller fees, and you reach people in your local area instantly.

The downside is that buyer protection is far weaker than Vinted or eBay — Facebook Marketplace has no built-in escrow or refund system the way those platforms do, so you're relying on in-person pickup and your own judgement.

For clothes specifically, Facebook Marketplace is fine for local bundle sales but worse than Vinted for reach and search. It also lacks the structured categories and buyer-protection rails that make Vinted safe.

body.heading: Other Vinted alternatives worth knowing
paragraphs: Shpock is a UK-focused local marketplace for buying and selling second-hand goods — closer to Facebook Marketplace than to Vinted, useful for local pickups and household items rather than fashion.

Oxfam Online and other charity shops have moved online, and they're a good *buying* alternative for second-hand clothes with the feel-good of a charity purchase — but they're not somewhere you can list your own items.

For high-end and luxury, Vestiaire Collective is the specialist alternative — it authenticates designer items, so it's the right place for luxury fashion where authenticity matters. For everyday clothes, Vinted remains the better fit.
In the US, Poshmark fills the Vinted role, but it has little UK presence, so it's rarely the right alternative for UK buyers and sellers.

body.heading: Which alternative is right for you?
paragraphs: Choose Depop if you sell vintage, streetwear or Y2K and want a fashion-focused audience. Choose eBay if you sell collectibles, electronics, or non-clothing items and want maximum reach. Choose Facebook Marketplace for bulky items and local cash sales.

Choose Vinted itself if you sell everyday branded clothes and want the simplest experience — no seller fees, integrated shipping, and a large UK fashion audience. The honest answer for many sellers is to use more than one.

One thing that holds true across all of them: [the fundamentals of selling second-hand](/guides/how-to-sell-on-vinted) — good photos, specific descriptions, and researched pricing — are the same everywhere. Master them once and you can list anywhere.

faq.question: What is the best alternative to Vinted in the UK?
faq.answer: Depop is the closest like-for-like alternative for fashion, with a younger, trend-driven audience and £0 seller fees since 2026. eBay is the best generalist alternative and is also free for private sellers. Which is 'best' depends on what you're selling.

faq.question: Is Depop or Vinted better?
faq.answer: Depop skews younger and more trend-driven (vintage, streetwear, Y2K), while Vinted is more mass-market and budget-focused. For everyday branded clothes, Vinted is usually better; for unique vintage or streetwear, Depop's audience may value it more. See our [Vinted vs Depop comparison](/guides/vinted-vs-depop).

faq.question: Is eBay free to sell on now?
faq.answer: Yes, for UK private sellers. Since October 2024, private sellers get 300 free listings a month with no final value fees. Fees apply if you exceed 300 listings, add optional upgrades, or deliver overseas.

faq.question: Are there any free alternatives to Vinted?
faq.answer: Yes — Vinted, Depop and eBay are all now effectively free for UK private sellers (eBay caps free listings at 300 a month). Facebook Marketplace is also free but has far weaker buyer protection.

faq.question: Can I sell on Vinted and Depop at the same time?
faq.answer: Yes, and many resellers cross-list on both. The audiences barely overlap, so it doubles your reach. The main risk is selling the same item twice, so keep your inventory in sync and delist immediately when something sells.
